If you're shopping for a dog tracker, Whistle isn't available to buy anymore. They shut down for good in 2025. No devices, app, or way to sign up, even if you wanted to.


The good news, though, is that everything you loved about Whistle is still very much available. This guide breaks down what happened to Whistle, how GPS dog tracking works, and how Life360 Pet GPS handles the job today so that you can find the right fit for your dog's particular brand of mischief.

## Is Whistle Even Around Anymore?


Nope. Whistle Labs built one of the first popular GPS trackers for dogs back in 2012, and Mars Petcare bought the company in 2016. For years, the two names sat together comfortably. Whistle stayed the pet-tech brand out front, while Mars kept the lights on in the background.


That changed in the summer of 2025. Tractive, an Austrian pet-tracking company, acquired Whistle from Mars Petcare, and they decided to shut down the entire platform rather than run two competing products side by side. Every Whistle device, including the Go, Go Explore, and Switch Fit, stopped tracking, syncing, and working on August 31, 2025.


Former Whistle customers were offered a free Tractive tracker and a transfer of any remaining subscription time, but that offer closed on September 30, 2025. If you missed it, or if you're only now noticing that your dog's collar has gone quiet, there's no way to reactivate the old device.


## How Dog GPS Trackers Work


A dog GPS tracker tells you where your dog is: it taps into satellites like the navigation app on your phone, just pointed at your dog instead of your commute. That location then travels to your phone over a cellular network.


The second part is everything built on top of that location. Safe zones that ping you when your dog leaves the yard. Alerts the moment they slip out. A history of where they've been. This is where trackers separate themselves, because raw coordinates on a map are only half the story. What you really want is to know the second something's wrong and be able to find them fast when it is.


Bluetooth-only trackers ping nearby phones to relay a location. That's handy when your dog is close, but the moment they wander past the range of the nearest phone, you're guessing again. For a dog who treats the fence line as a personal challenge, that's not enough coverage.


Both Whistle and Life360 Pet GPS use the full GPS-plus-cellular playbook. Here's how each one handles it.


## Whistle, the Tracker That Set the Standard


For a long stretch, Whistle was the name people reached for first, and here’s why.


### What Whistle Did Well


Whistle helped popularize the whole smart collar category. The Whistle Go Explore paired GPS location tracking with health and activity stats like step counts, calories burned, licking and scratching frequency, and sleep quality. It was basically a Fitbit that clipped onto your dog's collar. It leaned on GPS, WiFi, and AT&T's cellular network to keep tabs on your dog, and it let you set up safe zones that pinged you if your dog crossed the line.


The Whistle Go Explore claimed up to 20 days on a single charge, with charging recommended every 7 to 10 days for typical use. It also had a built-in nightlight to help you spot your dog after dark. For years, it was a strong tracker with a loyal following.


### The Catch With Whistle


The biggest problem? It doesn't exist anymore. Every one of those features shut down on August 31, 2025, and no amount of searching can bring a discontinued tracker back online. A sealed, never-opened Whistle device can't even be activated, because the servers that powered it are gone.


That leaves a problem for the pet parents who trusted it. The good part is that the things Whistle did well, like real-time GPS, dependable battery life, and safe-zone alerts, are exactly what a current tracker can still deliver.


## Life360 Pet GPS, Built for the Whole Family


Life360 Pet GPS takes the core job Whistle did, finding your dog in real time, and folds it into the app your family may already use for everything else.


### What Life360 Pet GPS Does Well


Life360 Pet GPS taps into satellites, cellular networks, WiFi, and Bluetooth Long Range to pinpoint your pet's location in real time, right on the same map as the rest of your Life360 Circle. Because it runs on cellular coverage rather than nearby phones, distance is rarely a problem, whether you've got a Great Dane or a small dog that can slip through a gap in a fence without anyone noticing.


The device clips onto most standard collars or harnesses in seconds. Add a Place in the Life360 app, like home, the dog park, or grandma's backyard, and you'll get an Escape Alert the moment your pet leaves it. If your dog does make a break for it, Life360's Pet Finder Network can notify nearby Life360 members with your pet's details, turning 100 million app users into an impromptu search party. It really does take a village, and now the village has your dog's photo.


Life360 Pet GPS runs up to 14 days on a single charge, and a built-in safety light helps you spot your dog on late-night walks. When the charge finally runs out, the tracker drops into a 6-month Bluetooth Reserve Mode instead of going fully dark, so your pet stays locatable at close range even with a dead battery. The device is IP68 water- and bite-resistant, too, sturdy enough for puddle jumps, backyard zoomies, and the occasional roll in the mud. (It works for cats as well, if your household has more than one species of escape artist.)


### The Catch With Life360 Pet GPS


Real-time tracking requires a Life360 Gold or Platinum membership, so there's an ongoing cost, but pretty much any other GPS tracker requires the same. Life360 Pet GPS also skips the in-depth health and fitness reporting that Whistle was known for. If daily vet-style wellness stats are your main goal, this isn't built for that. For finding your dog and knowing the moment they wander, though, it's the perfect fit.

## Why the Best Tracker Lives in One Family App


A tracker that sits in its own app, with its own login and notifications, becomes one more thing to juggle. Your dog's location is fixed. Your teen's location is in another. Your keys are in a third. Every where is it question sends you hunting through a different icon.


With Life360 Pet GPS, your dog shows up on the same map as the people you love and the stuff you're always misplacing. Slip a Tile tracker onto your keys and a Pet GPS onto your dog, and they'll land right alongside your family members in one app. Whistle's subscription was in its own silo. A Life360 Gold or Platinum membership covers your dog and also brings crash detection, emergency dispatch, 30 days of location history, and driving reports for everyone in your family.


A pet tracker will only answer where's my dog? but Life360 answers the bigger question running in the back of your mind anyway: where is everyone, and is everything okay?


## What It Costs


Whistle required its own standalone subscription, separate from anything else in your life, running up to about $99 a year for full tracking. That subscription is gone now, along with the devices it powered.


The Life360 Pet GPS tracker itself is $49.99. Location tracking comes included with a Life360 Gold or Platinum membership, and Gold runs around $12.49 a month on the annual plan built around the Pet GPS device. There's no separate monthly fee just for your dog. The first Pet GPS device activates for free, and adding a second costs a one-time $3.99 activation fee per Circle.


Instead of paying for a pet-only service, you're covering your whole family's safety, and your dog is included.


#### Not ready for GPS? Start with a Pet Tag.


A stainless steel QR tag gets your dog home fast if they wander off — one-time $7.99, no subscription required.


###
The Lower-Cost Option, Life360 Pet Tag


Not every dog needs live GPS. If what you really want is a way for a stranger to get your dog home fast, the[Life360 Pet Tag](https://www.life360.com/tile-trackers/product/pet-tag?icid=blog_whistle-vs-life360-pet) is the simpler play. It's a stainless steel ID tag with a QR code for a one-time $7.99 payment, with no subscription attached.


Whoever finds your dog points their phone camera at the tag, and the scan pings you via the Life360 Pet Finder Network, connecting you directly with the person standing next to your dog.


[Pet Tag and Pet GPS](https://www.life360.com/pet-safety?icid=blog_whistle-vs-life360-pet) aren't rivals. The Tag handles identification and recovery for a few bucks. The GPS handles knowing where your dog is right now, before anyone else has to find them at all. Plenty of pet parents run both, with the Tag on the collar as the safety net and the GPS as the early warning system.


## Which Tracker Should You Actually Get in 2026?


Whistle isn't one of your options in 2026, so the decision comes down to what you want a tracker to do.


If you want your dog's location to live in the same app as everyone else you're keeping tabs on, with real-time tracking, Escape Alerts, a community finding network, and a battery that keeps a reserve even after it dies, then Life360 Pet GPS is the pick for you. For most pet parents who came here looking for a Whistle replacement, the combination beats a standalone pet gadget.


Just want the cheapest, dependable way to get your dog home if they turn up two streets over? Start with the Pet Tag. It covers identification and recovery for $7.99 with no ongoing cost, and you can always add GPS later.


## **Finding Your Dog, Whistle-Free**


Whistle had a good decade-plus run, but what you need is a tracker that works today. Life360 Pet GPS gives you real-time location tracking, Escape Alerts, and a Pet Finder Network built on 100 million members, backed by a battery that keeps going even after the charge runs out. Because it lives inside the same app as the rest of your family's safety features, your dog isn't a separate subscription. They're just part of the map.

See where your dog, your kids, and your keys all live on one map. Real-time location, Escape Alerts, and a community that has your back.
